To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quaternary organization of oligomeric and complex enzymes is a consequence of the interplay between the thermodynamic forces of stabilization of the native state and the kinetic factors that control the rates of folding, assembly, and dissociation of the enzyme molecules.
the quaternary structures of enzymes are not random.

1) the quaternary structures of oligomeric and complex enzymes are determined by the number of protomers, their size, shape, and mutual disposition; 2) oligomeric enzymes have evolved from monomeric enzymes by gene duplication; and 3) complex enzymes are formed from monomeric and oligomeric enzymes by genetic fusion of their polypeptide chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the active sites and the mechanism by which they are regulated.
the quaternary organization of enzymes.
the quaternary structures of enzymes, the oligomeric enzymes, and complex enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quaternary level of organization in enzymes is of fundamental importance.
the quaternary structures of enzymes are not as diverse as the tertiary structures.
the quaternary structures of oligomeric and complex enzymes, like the tertiary structure of monomeric proteins, are the result of the interplay between the forces of attraction and repulsion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the presence of a quaternary structure in enzymes.
the quaternary structures of oligomeric and complex enzymes are determined by the same factors as the tertiary structures of monomeric enzymes, but the factors act on a much larger scale.
enzymes are not simple molecules but complex ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the quaternary structures of proteins can be very different, the underlying principles of protein folding and stability are the same.
the quaternary state of enzymes is an important determinant in the regulation of their catalytic activity.
the quaternary structures of enzymes are highly diverse, and the biological functions of enzymes can be highly diverse.
